messages.author: 146a54acf88740fd
messages.subject: non linear formula
parts:
Hi all,
How can I write a non-linear formula  to INLA? Here's a toy-set of my data.

Sunny regards,
Fabio

a=3
b=0.5
c=0.9

x = runif(100, min=0, max=6)
eta = a-b*exp(-c*x)

sd=0.03
Y = rnorm(length(x), mean=eta, sd=sd)
out= data.frame(x,Y)

library(ggplot2)
p = ggplot(data=out, aes(x=x,y=Y))
p = p + geom_point(size=3, shape=21, fill="white")
print(p)

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] non linear formula
parts:
On Sun, 2015-08-30 at 09:04 +1000, Daniel Simpson wrote:
> Nonlinear predictors are totally out of the scope for INLA. As far as
> I know, JAGS and STAN don't have specialised models for
> spatiotemporal data. They are both quite flexible, however, so it may
> be possible to implement one anyway.

inla can also have link-models, meaning link functions with parameters,
meaning that we could have the mean in the Gaussian (or something else)
to be

a + exp(linear.predictor)

which corresponds to your case. Here 'a' is unknown, probably positive.
this is a line of extention that is not yet fully explored, as link
functions can easily kill log-concavity of the likelihood contribution
(depending on the hyperparameters...)

so it depends on how your problem generalise...

H
